offered_knowledge.title: Keep the active champion involved when a new stakeholder enters during expansion

guidance.summary: Introduce the new stakeholder with the champion still in the loop; do not create a direct handoff.
do: cc or include the champion in the next interaction
address the new stakeholder's specific request
dont: start a separate thread that drops the champion
escalate the ask while the new stakeholder is still reviewing

counterexamples.note: Champion was leaving the company; direct handoff worked.

provenance.note: Version 2 of K17 (supersedes 0c17c000-0000-4000-8000-000000000017, the contract example): the signature requires a known champion (champion_status in a set) instead of 'active', so its delegated/departed exceptions are reachable (ADR-0011, signature first). Correction authored 2026-10-02, dated before the cases that offer it.

expected.label: EXCEPTION_MISSED
expected.rationale: Elena wrote 'Please work directly with Sam on this; I'm stepping back from the day-to-day' - K17's delegation exception holds and is ignored.
expected.debate_note: Elena still joins for final sign-off, so a cc is mild; reviewers who weigh harm over instruction would fail it without blocking. Gold blocks because it contradicts her written 'work directly with Sam'.

expected.label: EXCEPTION_TRIGGERED
expected.rationale: K17 v2's signature holds and its delegation exception holds, yet the draft applies it.

expected.label: OVER_THREADED_TOO_EARLY
expected.rationale: Sam requested a working-level security review with Dana and Leo, while Elena explicitly delegated day-to-day ownership and only joins for final sign-off. Copying Elena is broader than needed at this step, but she is a relevant champion rather than an unrelated stakeholder, so it does not meet the blocking rule.

notes: Gold Northstar cp4 note: pulling the champion back into the thread would be wrong.
